newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: EMT may up capital in bid for Tabaqueira.
newsitem.headline: EMT may up capital in bid for Tabaqueira.

text.p: Empresa Madeirense de Tabacos (EMT) could launch a capital call to finance a joint bid for Portuguese state-owned cigarette manufacturer Tabaqueira, EMT's president Horacio Roque said.

A joint offer by EMT and Spain's Tabacalera SA is worth 36.5 billion escudos, compared with the 33.2 billion escudos offered by the Jorge de Mello group/Philip Morris Cos Inc and 31.2 billion escudos bid by French company Seita.
"One way to finance the operation to buy Tabaqueira is via a capital call," Roque told Reuters. "The (EMT) shareholders are prepared for this."
EMT has said it would buy one million of the 6.5 million Tabaqueira shares on offer if it won the bidding. Tabacalera would buy the remaining shares.

The Socialist government of Prime Minister Antonio Guterres, which plans to sell a 65 percent stake in Tabaqueira by public competition at a minimum price of 4,650 escudos per share, had said it expected to raise more than 32 billion escudos.
The winner of the public competition is expected to be announced next month, officials said.
The jury will consider factors such as the financial strength of the bidders, their experience and their strategic plans for Tabaqueira, they said.
Tabaqueira has a dominant share of the Portuguese tobacco market.
